messages:
Lee (Support): OrionHealth reported recurring 429s + latency spikes on their Dedicated pool this morning. They say baseline qps ~65, hit bursts to ~420 for 8-12m and observed throttling + failed requests. Requesting urgent capacity help.
Jordan (SRE): Can you paste the customer's pool id and the time window? I'll check autoscale events.
Lee (Support): Pool id: dp-orion-12. Window: 2026-03-09 09:02 - 09:20 UTC. Customer says autoscale didn't add nodes, they saw steady CPU <40% but token queue length jumped.
Maya (Oncall): Looking at the cluster logs now. There's a spike in concurrent requests and small degradation in avg latency from 120ms to 1.3s around 09:04. No node provisioning events during the window.
Jordan (SRE): That's odd — autoscaler should respond. Two possibilities: cooldown misconfig or we hit burst cap for their SLA tier. @Ryan can you confirm dp-orion-12 autoscale policy?
Ryan (Infra): dp-orion-12 is on dedicated-reserved-2 (min=2, max=8), scale_up policy: +1 node per 60s with cooldown 600s. They also have burst_quota=2 nodes reserved for bursts but the pool was pinned to region-west-2 where physical capacity was constrained at the time.
Anita (CS): Customer insists their usage pattern is predictable. They had a marketing push they didn't tell us about. Wants recommendation for baseline vs peak sizing and to avoid future throttles.
Lee (Support): Error sample from customer (they sent request trace):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"pool throughput cap reached"}
```

Jordan (SRE): Two actionable items: 1) fix immediate customer outage (temporary mitigation) 2) long-term sizing & autoscale tuning. For 1) we can open a canary route to their dedicated pool to shift critical traffic to spare capacity in us-east-1. Need approval from infra to migrate traffic.
Ryan (Infra): We have spare compute in us-east-1 but cross-region routing will add ~40-80ms for some requests. If customer's SLO allows it, we can route high-priority routes. I'll prepare a runbook.
Maya (Oncall): Repro steps for our debugging team (quick):
1) Use their test API key (provided securely) and run 30s ramp from 10->500 qps hitting /v1/generate with their typical prompt size.
2) Capture queue_length, token_latency_p95, node_count, and autoscaler events.
Command snippet:
```
loadtest --rps 500 --duration 30s --url "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" --header "Authorization: Bearer <orion-test-key>" --body-file prompt.json
```

Lee (Support): Customer also reported a couple of auth 401s; those look like test keys hitting production routes while failing over. Might be unrelated but call it out.
Emma (Billing): Heads-up — if we propose raising baseline from 2->6 nodes we'll need an amended Dedicated contract (monthly commit change). I'll prepare pricing delta for CS to share.
Anita (CS): Customer will accept a PR to baseline if we can guarantee no more throttles during campaigns. They asked about predictive autoscale (pre-warm).
Jordan (SRE): Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) temporary scaling override to +4 nodes now (manual scale to 6) 2) reduce autoscale cooldown from 600s->120s 3) increase burst_quota to 4 for 72h 4) add queue-based scale trigger (token queue > 200 => scale).
Ryan (Infra): Manual scale executed: nodes=6 as of 1779992345. Will implement cooldown change and burst_quota for 72h. Noted physical capacity limits may still cap max nodes if region constrained.
deploy-bot: deploy started: infra/scale-runbook v2 -> applied to dp-orion-12 by Ryan at 1779992388
Maya (Oncall): Post-scale quick check: queue length dropped from 1200->40 within 45s, p95 latency back to ~160ms. No 429s since scale.
Lee (Support): Customer confirms reduced errors, thanks. They're asking for a recommended long-term config (baseline/peak/utilization).
Jordan (SRE): Sizing guidance we gave them: target steady-state utilization 40-60% CPU and token throughput to leave headroom for model context and KV cache misses. For their workload: baseline qps=65, avg tokens per request ~380 -> monthly throughput suggests baseline nodes=4 to hit 45% util and absorb 2x typical bursts. Peak planning: assume marketing bursts to 6x baseline for ~10 minutes -> set max=10 and enable pre-warm 20min before planned campaign.
Anita (CS): I'll propose a plan: baseline=4, max=10, autoscale cooldown=120s, burst_quota=4, pre-warm workflow. Customer wants a scheduled pre-warm API we can trigger before known campaigns.
Ryan (Infra): We can add a pre-warm endpoint in the Console and a CLI action: `redwood scale prewarm --pool dp-orion-12 --nodes 10 --duration 30m`. ETA for feature: 4 business days. Meanwhile we can manual pre-warm on request.
Emma (Billing): I'll attach pricing examples for baseline=4 vs baseline=6 and estimated overage for occasional peaks.
Jordan (SRE): Follow-ups: create internal ticket DED-4572 for the autoscaler cooldown anomaly and DED-4573 for adding queue-based triggers. Add customer-facing ticket ORION-112 for the proposed plan and contract change.
Lee (Support): Action items summarized: @Anita create customer plan + contract draft; @Emma pricing delta; @Ryan pre-warm runbook + implement cooldown/burst changes; @Jordan investigate autoscaler logs for missing scale events (DED-4572). I'll update ORION-112 and loop in the customer.
Anita (CS): I'll schedule a call with OrionHealth for tomorrow 16:00 UTC to walk through plan.
Maya (Oncall): Marking resolved for immediate outage — monitoring for 24h. If we see queue > 300 alert ops.
Lee (Support): Thanks everyone — closing internal thread. Will post update to ORION-112 when call is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
